new_findings.place: Pyramid of the Feathered Serpent, Ciudadela, Teotihuacan
new_findings.assertion: One surviving Feathered Serpent tenoned head on the west facade retains two obsidian disk eye inlays. Barnes's photograph documents this head only; it does not establish the total number of heads once inlaid.
new_findings.uncertainty: Whether other eroded heads held disks is an interpretation, not direct archaeological observation

new_findings.assertion: Author photographs and discussion document obsidian insets in Quetzalpapalotl patio-carved columns in three motifs: mythological bird eyes, separate eye disks, and profile mirror-bowl patterns in bird tails. Not all empty sockets prove original obsidian inlays.
new_findings.uncertainty: Profile mirror interpretation is iconographic; restoration history unexamined

secondary_research_lead.assertion: Barnes cites TMP TE 5 6G:N5W1 pyrite and slate concentration adjacent to obsidian working, but specialized mirror-workshop status is not excavationally confirmed.
secondary_research_lead.locator: Barnes 2024 pp.461–462, citing Turner 1992 and Carballo 2007
